methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ground Control Development is a seed-stage housing and construction technology company founded by Lizzy Manzi that has raised $2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five private construction-tech companies—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, ADMARES, and Hedral—with no directly comparable public companies available in this subsector.

The stage-progression method, the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints, uses the $2M total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage venture progression. This yields an implied valuation of $5M. The single-method triangulation produces a range of $4M (low) to $6M (high), with a median of $5M, reflecting reasonable variance around the base calculation.

The analysis supports a valuation in the $4M–$6M range, with $5M as the central estimate. Key uncertainties include the lack of observable transaction multiples or revenue data from the peer set, reliance on a single methodological anchor, and absence of public market comparables to stress-test assumptions. A more granular valuation would benefit from operational milestones, revenue trajectory, and transaction evidence from private peers in construction automation.
